subject: Mathematics
source: Original supplementary learning draft aligned to Class 6 Ganita Prakash Chapter 2 (fegp102.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Verify any school-specific edition before publication.
goals: Distinguish a line, line segment and ray.
Identify an angle’s vertex and arms.
Classify acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex angles by size.
Use a protractor carefully to measure an angle.
summary: Geometry describes shapes, positions and relationships. A line extends indefinitely in both directions, a line segment has two endpoints, and a ray begins at one point and continues in one direction. Angles are formed when two rays share an endpoint. Their size describes the amount of turn between the rays.

concepts.title: Lines, segments and rays
concepts.explanation: A line has no endpoints and extends both ways. A segment is the part between two endpoints. A ray has one endpoint and extends in one direction.
concepts.example: A ruler edge marked from A to B represents segment AB; the drawn part does not extend endlessly.

concepts.title: Understanding an angle
concepts.explanation: An angle is formed by two rays with a common endpoint. The common endpoint is the vertex and the rays are the arms. The angle measures the turn from one arm to the other.
concepts.example: In ∠ABC, B is the vertex because it is the middle letter.

concepts.title: Types of angles
concepts.explanation: An acute angle is less than 90°; a right angle is 90°; an obtuse angle is greater than 90° but less than 180°; a straight angle is 180°. A reflex angle is greater than 180° but less than 360°.

concepts.title: Measuring accurately
concepts.explanation: Place the protractor centre at the vertex, align its baseline with one arm, then read the scale that starts at 0° on that arm. Estimate whether the answer should be acute or obtuse before choosing a scale.
concepts.example: If the angle visibly opens wider than a right angle, a reading of 40° likely comes from the wrong scale.

workedExamples.question: Classify an angle measuring 35°.
steps: Since 35° is smaller than 90°, it is acute.

practice.question: What is the difference between a segment and a ray?
practice.answer: A segment has two endpoints; a ray has one endpoint and continues in one direction.
practice.why: The endpoints define how far each figure extends.

practice.question: Classify 90°, 180° and 215°.
practice.answer: 90° is right; 180° is straight; 215° is reflex.

practice.question: Why must the protractor centre sit on the vertex?
practice.answer: Because the measurement must be taken from the angle’s actual turning point.
practice.why: Misplacing the centre changes the alignment and can give a wrong reading.

practice.question: Can two angles have different arm lengths but the same measure?
practice.answer: Yes. Angle measure depends on the amount of turn, not the length of the arms.
practice.why: Extending an arm does not change the opening.

mcqs.why: Acute angles are greater than 0° and less than 90°.

mcqs.q: The common endpoint of an angle’s arms is its…
mcqs.why: The vertex is the shared endpoint.
A straight angle forms a straight line.
Angle measure represents the opening or turn.

revision: Line: extends both ways; segment: two endpoints; ray: one endpoint.
The vertex is the common endpoint of the two arms.
Acute < 90°; right = 90°; obtuse is between 90° and 180°; straight = 180°; reflex is between 180° and 360°.
When using a protractor, align the centre and baseline, then choose the correct scale.

chapterTest.instructions: Answer independently before opening the answer guide. Show steps for calculations.

questions.q: Explain the difference between a line, segment and ray.
questions.answer: A line extends in both directions; a segment has two endpoints; a ray has one endpoint and extends in one direction.

questions.q: List the steps to measure an angle with a protractor.
questions.answer: Place centre at vertex, align baseline with one arm, read the scale beginning at zero on that arm, and check whether the result matches the visible angle.
